statements.statement: The override vote failed, which the speaker said reflects a loss of public confidence rather than a messaging problem.
Middle school athletics were eliminated as a reduction from roughly a $29 million school budget following the failed override.
Chapter 70 funds cover 35% of the entire school budget in Lunenburg.
Referred again to 'the entire failure of the override' when saying this is the end of the road for further school cuts.
The deficit between what the town should be funding for schools and what it actually funds grows every year.
The cherry sheet in the Senate budget included an additional amount (heard as '$3 and $55,000') for Lunenburg, across a few departments.
The difference between the House budget figure (heard as $350,000) and the town's budget built on the Governor's proposal is $470,000.
Chapter 70 alone is about $9.8 million under the Governor's budget and $10.1 million under the Senate budget, roughly a $100,000 increase.
The town's MBTA assessment has doubled, contributing to higher estimated charges.
The town's budget was built on the Governor's FY27 number, with Lunenburg's state aid figure heard as '11,44917' and estimated charges heard as '1,69' before backing charges out.
The difference between the Governor's budget number and the Senate budget number (for state aid relevant to the school request) is $413,000.
A placeholder estimate of $300,000 was proposed as a safe figure for the additional state money the school committee will request via a special town meeting.

warnings.condition: if the district's financial challenges persist
warnings.prediction: All extracurricular activities, including all athletics, will be on the table for future reductions, which would result in a full dismantling of Lunenburg schools.
Things are going to be hard and start breaking, affecting many things parents, citizens, and students care about.
There will be 30 kids in a classroom next year.
There is nothing more that can be cut; this is the end of the road for further school budget cuts.
Budget uncertainty is costing the district teachers and staff members who are leaving for districts that fund schools adequately.
There is nothing left to cut next year; extracurriculars and athletics are on the table because the district is desperate and cannot sustain more cuts.
The town is basically grasping at straws with the unrestricted government aid estimate; it may not materialize as hoped.
